**Page:** National Construction Industry Wage Rate Survey, 2005  
**URL:** https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/060411/dq060411f-eng.htm

**Evidence**  
- **Survey year:** 2005  
- **Regions surveyed / data available for:**  
  - *British Columbia*  
  - *Northwest Territories*  
  - *Nunavut*  
- **Highest paid construction occupation in British Columbia:**  
  - *Elevator constructors – $36.35 per hour* (Showed as “electrical constructors who received$36.35 an hour on average …”)  
- **Lowest paid occupation in British Columbia:**  
  - *Trade helpers/labourers – $17.34 per hour*  
- **Highest paid occupation in Northwest Territories:**  
  - *Plumbers – $29.82 per hour*  
- **Lowest paid occupation in Northwest Territories:**  
  - *Trade helpers/labourers – $16.80 per hour*  
- **Highest paid occupation in Nunavut (lower population):**  
  - *Plumbers – $23.61 per hour*  
- **Lowest paid occupation in Nunavut:**  
  - *Trade helpers/labourers – $16.94 per hour*  
- **Survey scope note (2006 preview):**  
  - “The next round of the survey will be conducted in 2006 and will cover Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick.”  
- **Publication date of this page:** 11 April 2006

**Coverage**  
The page provides wage‑rate data for the construction industry in three Canadian jurisdictions (British Columbia, Northwest Territories, Nunavut) for the year 2005.  
It does **not** contain any information about the number of people employed in construction or manufacturing, nor does it provide any population counts at the national or geographical level for 2006, 2008, 2016, or any other year referenced in the original question.  
Coverage is therefore **sub‑set** of the requested fields: only wage‑rate measurements for the three regions in 2005.

**Missing**  
All of the following requested fields are not established by this page (unknown on this page):  
- 2006 national construction worker count (≈700‑800 k)  
- 2008 national construction worker count (≈800‑900 k)  
- 2006 construction worker count in geography X (≈350‑450 k)  
- 2006 construction worker count in geography Y (≈170‑200 k)  
- 2008 construction worker increase in geography Y (≈30‑40 k)  
- 2016 national manufacturing worker count (≈1.8‑1.9 M)  
- 2017 & 2018 national manufacturing worker decrease  
- 2016 manufacturing worker count in geography X (≈900‑1000 k)  
- 2017 & 2018 manufacturing worker decrease in geography X  

**Next links** (potential routes that could provide missing data)  
1. **Link to the 2006 Wage Rate Survey page** (URL suggested by the text: “The next round of the survey will be conducted in 2006…”) – could potentially provide 2006 data.  
2. **Links to Statistics Canada “Daily Quotidien” archives** or “National Construction Industry Wage Rate Survey” series pages – may lead to detailed employment statistics.  
3. **Stats Canada “Search” or “Data” sections** – general navigation to workforce or industry census tables for Canada (potential for constructing national counts).  


**Status:** partial (page provides wage‑rate data only; no requested population or manufacturing figures found).
